newsitem.title: USA: US CRUDES STRENGTHEN, REFINER BUYING BOOSTS GRADES.
newsitem.headline: US CRUDES STRENGTHEN, REFINER BUYING BOOSTS GRADES.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf strengthened Tuesday afternoon in both outright and domestic grade markets, pushing differentials to firmer levels, traders said.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood 25 cents higher at $19.90-20.00 a barrel, approaching session plateaus.

Grade barrel business quieted from the morning, but gains made by both sweet and sour sectors remained. Latest talk in the Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James market saw premiums advance to 17-20 cents over September WTI, five cents better than late Monday.
West Texas Sour/Midland lopped off some of its discount to the September WTI, making a move to around minus $1.43-40, after selling to its strongest level at $1.43.
Grade dealers said sweet crudes advanced on stronger Dated Brent numbers in the North Sea, while sour moves were more a function of refiners stepping in and filling barrel needs.
"What you had was a large refiner stepping in the market early and started the buying of WTS," said a Texas trader.
Tonight's American Petroleum Institite (API) data was expected to show crude stocks down 1.75 million barrels, gasoline down 2 million barrels and refinery utilization rates down 0.50 pct.
